subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should direct `CronService.add` and declarative convergence own implicit delivery defaulting, or must all supported creation paths pass through the canonical cron normalization boundary?
rationale: Both designs can produce the requested behavior, but choosing the permanent ownership boundary affects compatibility and whether OpenClaw keeps one or multiple sources of delivery policy.

options.title: Centralize shared policy
options.body: Extract one shared delivery-default rule used by normalization and direct-service creation, retaining announce defaults for `isolated`, `current`, and `session:*`.

options.title: Normalize every caller
options.body: Keep delivery defaulting solely in `normalizeCronJobCreate` and update direct-service/declarative callers to use that boundary before persistence.

options.title: Keep direct callers explicit
options.body: Leave direct-service callers without implicit delivery and document that they must always provide delivery configuration.

recommendation.title: Centralize shared policy
recommendation.body: Extract one shared delivery-default rule used by normalization and direct-service creation, retaining announce defaults for `isolated`, `current`, and `session:*`.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged cron session-target restoration established the surrounding product contract and owner boundary.
